key_insight: Multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence can non-destructively distinguish interfacial from bulk degradation in perovskite solar cells and reveals that PEABF4 initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but later accelerates depth-spreading recombination losses under heat.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic for tracking where degradation begins and how it propagates, helping engineers compare passivation strategies and aging stability in perovskite device stacks.
method: Use wavelength-dependent PL excitation to probe different depths non-destructively.
Compare PL decay signatures before and after thermal aging in PEABF4-treated stacks.
Fit diffusion-recombination simulations to interpret surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PL measurements showed reduced interfacial recombination after PEABF4 treatment, but faster degradation under thermal stress with losses broadening from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber, supported by simulation.
watch_item: PL-based depth interpretation depends on model assumptions and careful calibration, so changes in excitation response should be validated against complementary degradation measurements.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
